findings.title: Deploy will hard-fail at container start unless CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS and/or COOKIE_SECURE secrets are populated — new behaviour introduced by the C1 remediation, after the deploy pipeline (Task 9) was written and last exercised
findings.expected: poshivon_app starts on prod with the secrets currently configured in the repository's GitHub environment
findings.actual: server/internal/config/config.go:107-119 now returns an error from Load() when CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS contains no non-empty CSV entry AND COOKIE_SECURE is false, for any APP_STORAGE other than 'memory'. deploy.yml hardcodes APP_STORAGE: mysql (line ~100), so prod always takes the hard-fail branch, not the warn-only one. Both values come from optional GitHub secrets (deploy.yml:110-111); if either is unset the secret expands to an empty string and the app exits at startup instead of serving.
findings.reproduction: Set CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS='' and COOKIE_SECURE=false with APP_STORAGE=mysql, then call config.Load() — it returns 'config: CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS пуст и COOKIE_SECURE=false ...; задайте оба значения явно (APP_STORAGE="mysql")'. Covered by TestLoad_OriginFallbackGuard, which passes — the behaviour is intentional and fail-loud, not a code defect. The risk is operational: this is a new precondition on the deploy that did not exist when Task 9's pipeline was last validated.
findings.recommendation: Before Wave 12, confirm in GitHub repository settings that secrets CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (the real prod origin, e.g. https://<domain>) and COOKIE_SECURE=true are both set. This is a pre-deploy checklist item for the user, not a code change. Not classified critical because the failure is loud, immediate, and occurs before any traffic is served.

findings.title: Three Phase-1 acceptance criteria are client-side and have no automated coverage — verified by code inspection only
findings.expected: Every acceptance criterion is backed by an automated test
findings.actual: TS-16 (OAuth state mismatch aborts login), TS-19 (no /settings, /chats, /calculations requests before the access gate resolves) and TS-20 (non-admin does not see the «Пользователи» nav item) are enforced entirely in client/src and there is no client test runner, so they were verified by reading the code paths rather than by executing them.
findings.reproduction: client/package.json declares no test script; grep for *.test.jsx / *.spec.jsx in client/src returns nothing. The three code paths are unambiguous conditionals (AuthCallback.jsx:56, Panel.jsx:260/310 guarded on status==='ready', Panel.jsx:627/895 guarded on isAdmin) and each has independent server-side enforcement, which is why this is minor rather than major.
findings.recommendation: Known and accepted gap — tech-spec's Client tests section and tasks/13.md both state client unit tests are out of scope for Phase 1, and Tasks 7-8 covered these via Verify-user. Live confirmation is listed under deferredToPostDeploy. If a client test runner is introduced in Phase 2, these three are the highest-value first tests.

findings.title: The shared poshivon_test database's schema_migrations table records only 001_auth_sessions, although all six migrations' objects are present
findings.actual: SELECT version FROM schema_migrations on poshivon_test returns only '001_auth_sessions', while access_requests, the role/has_access columns and the seeded admins are all present.
findings.reproduction: docker exec poshivon_db mariadb -uroot -proot poshivon_test -e "SELECT version FROM schema_migrations;"
findings.recommendation: No action needed — this is an artefact of the local/CI test fixture, not of the product. Both this QA run and .github/workflows/test.yml deliberately apply server/migrations/*.up.sql with the mariadb client rather than through migrations.Run, so the bookkeeping table is not written. Production applies migrations via migrations.Run on app start, and that path's bookkeeping is covered by TestAdminSeed_SurvivesCollisionUnderLegacyCollation_ViaRun, which asserts schema_migrations is written and that a repeated Run is idempotent. Recorded so a future reader does not mistake it for a missed migration.
